posts.cooked:
An idea that struck me the other day after playing a couple rounds of games -- has anyone thought out/tried a competitive game? Two teams of heroes against one another, with no villain? What kind of modifications, if any, would be needed to balance this sort of thing? Off the top of my head, I imagine it'd have to work like the Vengeance pack, where the players of different teams alternate instead of all of them going, then all the others going.

Thoughts?

posts.name: cmschex
posts.cooked:
mwc146:

 

Pydro wrote:
There was a forum game like that, it didn't work out so well.  
What happened?

 

The game is just not balanced that way so leads to broken combos.  In the forum game it was thematic Ww2 Bunker, AG Legacy, Argent vs Chrono, Omni X and (cant remember 3rd one).  Ongoing/Equip Destruction was really powerful, extra power usage could essntially shut down other heroes.  Incap abilities had the same potential as well and a lot of cards have to have an impartial judge to rule on them.  So, in short, it can work, but don't expect an especially gun or balanced experience.  Play Tactics

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Hero vs hero is never more than a fun and unbalanced side game, but it can work.

The games that woek best are 3v3, or 3 hero free for all.

How we do it:

Villain and non-hero refer to any hero not on your team, hero refers only to heroes on your team.

Ongoing destruction can also destroy equipment.

The environment deck treats all targets as hero and villain targets, if there are seperate effects (pillars of hercules) for villain and hero only do the hero one.

There's a lot of on the spot rules we make to help balance, and certain cards are not allowed, like takedown, if you draw it you put it in the trash and draw the next.

It only works as a friendly diversion, if people get competetive it goes bad really quickly.

I had the same thought about Civil War and SotM, then a forum search led me here.

Arcanist Lupus:

Yes. It's called Tactics.

What if Tactics isn't your thing? What if you wanted the card game experience, but with hero v. hero? 

And remember, before Vengeance (and later Villains), the only way to play was hero team vs. 1 villain.

It's possible to be done, and done well. Unfortunately, I think it is unlikely in any official capacity.
